turns.content: For particles selected near the Maxwell mean speed, derive how de Broglie wavelength scales with particle mass m and source temperature T.
For two runs in which the second particle mass is twice the first, use the mass-temperature scaling to express lambda2/lambda1 in terms of T1/T2.

For a single slit, use the usual side-maximum approximation a sin(theta_j) approximately (j+1/2)lambda. Use the first side maximum at 15 degrees in run 1 and the second at 20 degrees in run 2 to find lambda2/lambda1.
Combine the wavelength ratio obtained from diffraction with the mass dependence of the thermal de Broglie wavelength to determine the source-temperature ratio.
Show explicitly how the mass-temperature scaling and diffraction-derived wavelength ratio determine T1/T2.
Using the diffraction model selected above, state its approximation level and, where appropriate, compare it with the exact stationary-point locations to establish the reporting precision.
Using the comparison between the side-maximum approximation and the exact stationary-point locations, report the alternative temperature-ratio estimate with justified precision.
Report the final temperature ratio and summarize the thermal-wavelength scaling and diffraction relation used.
